items.title: "Three not one more" and "Eight Whatevers": Memorize these eleven sentences and you will be 80% protected from scams
items.core: All telecom and internet scams have just four words at the end: They ask you to transfer money. The Ministry of Public Security has condensed tens of millions of cases into two sets of formulas, which can be memorized by primary school students and even by an 80-year-old man.
body: Explanation: All telecommunications network frauds have only four words at the end: asking you to transfer money. The Ministry of Public Security has condensed tens of millions of cases into two sets of formulas, which can be memorized by primary school students and even by an 80-year-old man. Do not click on unknown links; do not trust unknown calls; do not disclose personal information; verify transfers and remittances.
Chapter: [Three Nothings, One More: General Outline] [Eight Everythings: One Size Fits All]

Routines: 1️⃣ Anyone who claims that the public security bureau or law requires remittance is a scam! 2️⃣ Anyone who asks you to transfer money to a "safe account" is a scam! 3️⃣ Anyone who notifies you of winning a prize or requires you to pay money first is a scam! 4️⃣ Anyone who notifies "family members of an accident" and asks you to remit money first is a scam! 5️⃣ Anyone who asks for bank card information and SMS verification code is a scam! 6️⃣ Anyone who asks you to open online banking and accept "fund inventory" is a scam! 7️⃣ Anyone who claims to be a leader (boss) and asks for remittance is a scam! 8️⃣ Any unfamiliar website (link) that asks to register bank card information is a scam!
Pitfalls: ❌ Scammers will tell you "we are the exception": this case is special, this platform is special, this claim settlement is special - no exceptions, not one.

Warning: ⚠️ The routines will be upgraded and re-skinned: rebates for fake orders, fake investments, cancellation of campus loans, AI face-swapping, FaceTime calls... The shell is always new, and the core is always "give sweetness or intimidation first, and finally let you transfer money".
Defense: 🛡️ If you encounter any uncertainty, call 96110 to ask first, and then decide whether to take action - this sentence is more important than a mantra.
Law: ⚖️ The "Anti-Telecommunications and Internet Fraud Law" has been implemented: providing bank cards, phone cards, and technical support for fraud are illegal acts, so don't get involved in both.
Xingnao: 🛑 Send these two sets of formulas to everyone in the family, especially parents - they cannot remember "helping and trusting", but remember "everything... is a scam".

Case: Xiao Wang, a college student, received the text message "Pay tax first if you win". He remembered the "Eight Whatever" formula that said, "Anyone who has to pay money first to win a lottery is a scam." He directly deleted the text message and reported it, saving the 8,000 yuan he planned to pay for tuition.
items.remember: Send these two sets of formulas to everyone in the family, especially parents - they can't remember "it's a crime to help", but they can remember "everything... is a scam".

items.title: Liars cannot hypnotize, but they have five skills: intimidation, authority, greed for profit, urgency, and isolation
items.core: Why are highly educated people also deceived? Because scammers don't compete with your IQ at all, they attack your emotions. If you understand this psychological manipulation technique, you will be vaccinated against it.
body: Explanation: Why are highly educated people also cheated? Because scammers don't compete with your IQ at all, they attack your emotions. If you understand this psychological manipulation technique, you will be vaccinated against it. "You are suspected of money laundering" "Your child was in a car accident" "Your account will be frozen in two hours" - first scare you. When people are in fear, their rational brain will go offline directly, leaving only the thought of "solve it quickly". Police uniform, police officer certificate, wanted order, "Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission", "Prosecutor" - when you wear the vest of authority, you will be embarrassed to question and dare not refute, and you can only obey the "instructions". A small rebate, a 300 yuan claim, a free crab card - let you taste the sweetness first, and you will take the initiative to defend the "bigger sweetness next time": "The above are all true." "Automatic deduction if you don't handle it today" "Verification code is valid within 5 minutes" "The flight will close the claim channel immediately" - all the urgings are to not leave you time to verify and calm down. "The case is confidential and you are not allowed to tell anyone, including your family." "Only contact me through a single line." Cutting off the verification channel between you and the outside world is a standard feature of all brainwashing scams (including the northern Myanmar campus).
Routines: 1️⃣ Creating panic 2️⃣ Authoritative oppression 3️⃣ Small profit temptation 4️⃣ Time pressure 5️⃣ Isolation control
Pitfalls: ❌ The two most feared actions of scammers: hanging up the phone and talking to family members. So their words are all "can't hang up" and "can't speak".
Warning: ⚠️ Pay attention to a counter-intuitive fact: the more you think "I will definitely not be cheated", the more dangerous it is - confident people are undefended.

Defense: 🛡️ There is only one way to break the law: stop for three minutes before encountering. Hang up the phone, take a drink of water, tell someone what happened, or call 96110 - no matter how sophisticated the deception is, you are still afraid of "calm down for three minutes".
Law: ⚖️ Requesting property by means of intimidation or threats may constitute the crime of extortion; anyone who pretends to be a staff member of a state agency to defraud will be severely punished.
Xingnao: 🛑 Please forward this article to the family member who always says "I will not be cheated" - never be blindly confident, scammers only pick out unsuspecting people.

Case: Mr. Wang received a call from the Social Security Bureau saying that his account was involved in the case and requested that the money be transferred to a safe account. He remembered that scammers often used intimidation tactics and deliberately asked for details, but the other party hung up hastily. After checking, Mr. Wang confirmed that it was a fraud.
items.remember: Please forward this article to the family member who always says "I will not be cheated" - never be blindly confident, scammers only pick out unsuspecting people.

items.title: Attention iPhone users! With a FaceTime video, the "police officer" can put on a fake police uniform
items.core: There is a feature that Apple phone users should pay attention to recently: FaceTime. After the scammer discovered that he could change the display nickname at will, he turned it into a new channel for deception - the nickname was changed to "XX City Public Security Bureau", the avatar was changed to a police badge, and a video call was made, and there was even a "police officer in police uniform" sitting on the screen.
body: Explanation: Apple mobile phone users should pay attention to a feature recently: FaceTime. After the scammer discovered that he could change the display nickname at will, he turned it into a new channel for deception - the nickname was changed to "XX City Public Security Bureau", the avatar was changed to a police badge, and a video call was made, and there was even a "police officer in police uniform" sitting on the screen. Users can set the display nickname of FaceTime by themselves, and there is no threshold to change it to "XX Public Security" or "XX Anti-Fraud Center" - even the Hangzhou police have been impersonated by "Li Gui". The other party wears a "police uniform", gives your name and police number, presents a "Criminal Arrest Warrant" with your own ID number, claims that you are suspected of money laundering, and requires cooperation in "online handling of the case" and downloading a designated App - screen sharing is their "law enforcement recorder". He was asked to provide bank cards under his name for "checking transactions" and to transfer funds to a "safe account" to prove his innocence. During this period, he repeatedly emphasized that "the case is confidential and must not be disclosed to anyone." Someone discovered three hours later that more than 70,000 yuan had been transferred from Cali. In the same channel, there are also performances such as "WeChat customer service will help you cancel the one million protection deduction" and "bank customer service will cancel your loan account" - the communication method has been changed, but the core of the conversation has not changed at all.

Routines: 1️⃣ Change nicknames at will, pretend to be official at will 2️⃣ "Police uniform" and "arrest warrant" appear in the video 3️⃣ "Clear suspicion" requires transfer of money 4️⃣ Change vest and continue
Pitfalls: ❌ The Public Security Bureau does not handle cases by phone, video, or "online", there is no "safe account", and it will not let you transfer money to "prove your innocence".

Warning: ⚠️ How to identify: Normally, the home address is displayed above the incoming call, and the answer button is the phone icon; "FaceTime Video" is displayed above the FaceTime call, the background is the front camera screen, and the answer button is the camera icon.

Defense: 🛡️ Hang up an unfamiliar FaceTime call directly; users who do not use this function, please open iPhone "Settings" → "FaceTime" → turn it off. 🛡️ Any calls claiming to be from the Public Security Bureau or platform customer service should be verified through official channels and do not trust the caller ID.

Law: ⚖️ Pretending to be a staff member of a state agency and committing fraud constitutes the crime of fraud and shall be severely punished; using this to defraud property constitutes the crime of fraud.
Xingnao: 🛑 Help the elders at home to turn off FaceTime. This action only takes ten seconds - someone in the community has already been fooled.

Case: Ms. Li received a FaceTime video call. The caller's nickname was "Shenzhen Public Security Bureau" and she was wearing a police uniform. She falsely claimed that she was suspected of money laundering and requested video review. Ms. Li was suspicious and hung up. She called 110 to verify and confirmed that it was a scam.
items.remember: Any calls claiming to be from the Public Security Bureau or platform customer service should be verified through official channels and do not trust the caller ID.

items.title: "Turn on screen sharing to help you operate" - what is shared is not the screen, but your bank card
items.core: It doesn't matter if you are not proficient in operation, I will assist you remotely. Download this conferencing software, turn on screen sharing, and I will teach you step by step. "
body: Explanation: "It doesn't matter if you are not familiar with the operation, I will assist you remotely. Download this conferencing software, turn on screen sharing, and I will teach you step by step. "When you hear this, please hang up immediately. Because from the moment you click "Share Screen", everything on your phone is live broadcast in front of the scammer. After screen sharing is turned on, every frame displayed on your screen is synchronized to the other party in real time: the bank card password you enter, every text message verification code you receive, your balance, and your online loan limit - all are visible. Do you think it's safe if you don't "tell" him the verification code? Wrong. When sharing the screen, the text message pop-up window is displayed directly on your screen, and the scammer can see it clearly, and you don't need to read it at all. Impersonating the customer service to "cancel the account" requires sharing, pretending to be a police officer to "check the assets", and "the tutor will guide you to operate" also requires sharing - all of them require you to turn on screen sharing. When you find something wrong, just return to the home screen or switch to another app. It's useless, the sharing may still continue in the background. The correct operation is to click the "Stop Sharing" button in the conference software; when the phone has been remotely controlled, force shut down or remove the card to stop the loss.
Routine: 1️⃣ How to make clairvoyance 2️⃣ Why the verification code is lost 3️⃣ The script is the same 4️⃣ There is a way to exit
Pitfalls: ❌ "Sharing the screen does not affect the security of your funds" and "This is just a normal function of video conferencing" - every sentence is a line that makes you relax your vigilance.

Warning: ⚠️ The general version of the scam will also be disguised as "collaborative assistant", "remote guidance" and "after-sales assistance", and the App can be downloaded normally from the app store, which is extremely confusing.

Defense: 🛡️ Do not enable screen sharing with strangers under any circumstances; regular customer service, police, and banks will not make this request. 🛡️ If the other party prompts you to "operate your phone while talking", please terminate the call immediately and call official customer service or 96110 for verification.

Law: ⚖️ Using screen sharing to obtain verification codes to steal funds constitutes the crime of theft or fraud; developing and disseminating fraud-related remote control tools constitutes the crime of assisting information network criminal activities.
Xingnao: 🛑 Please remember one sentence: as soon as the screen is shared, the password verification code will run naked - the four words "stop sharing" can save your savings at the critical moment.

Case: An elderly man living alone received a call from the ‘police’, asking him to download conferencing software and share his screen to cooperate with the investigation. The old man pretended to operate and secretly asked his grandson to enter the verification code incorrectly on purpose. He took the opportunity to hang up and call the police, thus saving his pension money.
items.remember: Please remember one sentence: as soon as the screen is shared, the password verification code will run naked - the four words "stop sharing" can save your savings at the critical moment.

items.title: "The product you bought exceeds the formaldehyde limit, double refund" - the refund that comes to you on your own initiative will be charged to your deposit

The sleep you purchased The clothes have been found to have excessive formaldehyde. The company will now pay you three times the compensation. Please cooperate with me. "
body: Note: Not long after I finished my online purchase, I received a call: "Hello, this is the customer service of XX store. The pajamas you purchased have been found to have exceeded the standard. The company will now give you three times the compensation. Please cooperate with me." The other party knows what you bought, when you bought it, and where the delivery address is - because your order information has long been packaged and sold to the black market by the insider. The product name, order number, and delivery information are all correct. You naturally think: "This must be real customer service." "The system is busy and the claim cannot be processed" - the other party guides you to download the "Official Claims App", log in to the "Customer Service Online" webpage (all phishing pages), or start a video conference for "remote assistance". The bank card number, password, and SMS verification code are all "verified" in the past. Some require you to do "face recognition" and "identity confirmation" - at this point, your account is already open. After the balance in the card becomes empty, the other party will induce you to borrow money from various online loan platforms and then transfer money on the grounds that "the repayment ability needs to be verified for compensation" and "the refund channel is abnormal". The victim not only loses his deposit, but also carries a debt "from his own loan".

Routine: 1️⃣ Accurate order declaration, win people's trust 2️⃣ If the compensation is stuck, switch to the "official channel" 3️⃣ Take away the three-piece suit 4️⃣ Don't even miss the online loan limit
Pitfalls: ❌ "We take the initiative to pay, you don't have to spend a penny" - the first half of the sentence is bait, and the second half is fishhook.

Warning: ⚠️ Variations of the same script: compensation for lost express delivery, refund for member recharge errors, compensation for delayed air tickets, recall for product quality issues...the core is exactly the same.

Defense: 🛡️ Platform customer service will not take the initiative to handle refunds over the phone. All refunds will be returned via the original route within the shopping platform. You will never be asked to download an app, share your screen, or provide a verification code. 🛡️ When you receive a call from "customer service", please hang up and open the official app to check the order and refund status; if you are not sure, call 96110.

Law: ⚖️ E-commerce and logistics "insiders" who illegally sell citizens' order information constitute the crime of infringing on citizens' personal information and are severely punished; downstream gangs that commit fraud will be punished as fraud.
Xingnao: 🛑 Please keep this iron rule in mind: before the money arrives, any compensation that asks you to "operate first", "verify first" or lend it out first is digging a hole for you.

Case: After making an online purchase, Ms. Zhao received a call from ‘customer service’ saying that the product had excessive formaldehyde and required a triple refund. The other party sent her a QR code asking her to fill in her bank card information. Ms. Zhao remembered the refund process on the official platform. After logging into the store to verify, she found it was a fraud.

items.title: The teacher posted "collection of data fees" in the parent group in the early morning, and more than 30 parents transferred money in half an hour? The "class teacher" in the group may be fake
items.core: A notice suddenly popped up in the class group: "Dear parents, the materials fee/physical examination fee for this semester is several hundred yuan per person. Please scan the QR code to transfer it to the designated account. The deadline is today."
body: Description: A notice suddenly popped up in the class group: "Parents, the materials fee/physical examination fee for this semester is several hundred yuan per person. Please scan the QR code to transfer it to the designated account. The deadline is today." The avatar and name were exactly the same as those of the class teacher. Parents started to transfer money one after another, and dozens of people paid within ten minutes. By the time the real teacher saw it in the morning, the liar had already left the group and ran away. 👇 Scammers use small accounts to scan QR codes or steal parent accounts to sneak into the class group. They don’t speak for a while and look through historical messages and group announcements to find out the teacher’s speaking habits and charging rhythm. Change the avatar and nickname to be exactly the same as the class teacher, and send "charge notices" to the group in the early morning, during class, and when the teacher is busy. Send a QR code for payment, emphasizing that "the deadline is today, and the number of places is limited." They also arrange for child care to take the lead in transferring funds and send "paid" to create pressure to conform. As soon as the money was collected, the account was quickly dismissed and the group chat was withdrawn. By the time parents and teachers reacted, it was already too late. - The school charges fees through formal channels, and teachers will not use personal payment codes or private accounts to collect data fees in the group; - Parents should not rush to forward the notice of charges in the group, but verify it by phone, in person, or by private chatting with the teacher (note that scammers may steal the account at the same time, it is best to call to confirm); - Group management turns on "invitation confirmation, real-name review" and regularly removes unfamiliar members. Anyone who temporarily sends a QR code in the group and urges them to pay "data fees, physical examination fees, and insurance fees" should verify it first before transferring money. One phone call can stop most fake teachers.

Sobering up: 🛑 Sobering summary

In 2026, embassies and consulates abroad repeatedly reminded: This is a "virtual kidnapping" specifically targeting international students. In fact, nothing happened to the child! 👇 The scammers pretended to be domestic public prosecutors, embassies and consulates, and immigration bureaus, saying that the international students were "suspected of money laundering and identity fraud", and issued forged arrest warrants and arrest warrants, which scared people. On the grounds that the "case is confidential", students were asked to cut off contact with family and friends, hide in hotels or other places alone, and not tell anyone. They coaxed and coerced the students into taking photos and videos of themselves being kidnapped, hooded, and crying for help. The scammers even asked them to read a "ransom message." The scammers took the video and directly contacted the parents: "Your child is in our hands, and we will pay the ransom immediately. Don't call the police, otherwise we will cancel the case." "When parents see their children's faces and hear their cries, they often transfer money in a hurry without having time to verify it. - Real police officers will not handle cases over the phone or online, will not issue "wanted orders" to scare people, and will not ask for transfers to "safe accounts"; - Upon receiving news of "kidnapping", first try to contact the child himself, classmates, school or international student management teacher through other channels, or contact the embassy or consulate abroad (Consular Protection Hotline of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs 12308); - Tell your children: When you receive a phone call "involved in a crime", hang up and contact your family, and never cooperate with "disconnecting or taking videos". "Virtual kidnapping" deceives parents. The more "uncontactable" the child is, the more they need to calmly verify. Before confirming that the child is really in trouble, don't transfer any ransom money.

items.title: Can the credit report be "cleaned" by spending money? The central bank manages it uniformly, and even gods can't change it
items.core: There are overdue records on the credit report, and the mortgage cannot be approved, and you are too anxious to sleep. At this time, you saw an advertisement: "Credit report repair, internal channels, eliminate overdue credit, no fee if unsuccessful." "
body: Explanation: There is an overdue record on your credit report, and the mortgage cannot be approved. You are so anxious that you can't sleep. Then you see an advertisement: "Credit report repair, internal channels, eliminate overdue, no fee if unsuccessful. "You are excited. The intermediary asks you to provide your ID card, detailed credit report, and pay a few thousand yuan in "service fees," and then... "under review," "the process is complicated," "add more money to expedite it," until you find out that you have been blacklisted. Give the other party your ID card, bank card, and detailed credit report from the People's Bank of China - this is your most core personal information package, which may be resold, abused, or even used to saddle you with unknown debts. Down payments, expedited fees, channel fees, deposits... Scammers are well aware of "sunk costs": the more you pay, the more reluctant you are to stop. "Credit information updates have a cycle, please wait" - after a few months, you find that the record has not moved, and the other party has lost contact. Some intermediaries will instigate you to forge hospitalization certificates, bankruptcy documents or even official seals of state agencies to "complain" - before the credit report is completed, you will first be suspected of forging official documents and seals, turning from a victim into a suspect.
Routines: 1️⃣ Collect materials and extract information in depth 2️⃣ Increase the number of charges 3️⃣ Drag word tricks 4️⃣ More dangerous "professional operations"

Pitfalls: ❌ "There are people on the inside", "Central Bank relations", "Overdue records can be eliminated by spending money" - the credit information system is uniformly managed by the People's Bank of China, and no institution or individual has the right to modify or delete real bad records.

Warning: ⚠️ There is only one correct rule: true overdue records will be retained for 5 years from the date the debt is paid off, and will be automatically deleted upon expiration. There is no expediting and no manual removal.

Prevention method: 🛡️ If you have any questions about your credit report, only check through the official channels of the People's Bank of China; for erroneous records, you can apply for correction for free through the formal "Credit Report Objection" procedure - there is no charge for objection application, and those who charge are all scams. 🛡️ Never hand over the original credit report to any "repair agency". Once personal information is released, there will be endless consequences.

Law: ⚖️ Defrauding money in the name of credit repair constitutes the crime of fraud, and there have been cases in many places; abetting the forgery of certification documents is suspected of the crime of forging official documents and seals of state agencies.
Xingnao: 🛑 One sentence: You can’t clean up your credit report. If it’s overdue for 5 years, anyone who says it can be changed is a liar.

Case: Mr. Chen found an advertisement for "Credit Report Repair" because his credit card was overdue. After paying a service fee of 8,000 yuan, the other party lost contact. He went to the central bank to check and found that the records were still there. After calling the police, he found that the company had already been included in the list of abnormal operations.
items.remember: Never give the original credit report to any "repair agency". Once your personal information is released, there will be endless consequences.

items.title: "Cancel the campus loan account, otherwise it will affect your credit report"? Five years after graduation, there are still people who have been recruited.
items.core: Hello, I am a staff member of XX Banking Regulatory Commission. If you have registered a campus loan account while you were in school, you must cancel it according to national regulations. Otherwise, your personal credit will be affected, and you may even be included in the list of dishonest people. "
body: Explanation: "Hello, I am a staff member of the XX Banking Regulatory Commission. You have registered a campus loan account while you were in school. According to national regulations, you must cancel it. Otherwise, your personal credit will be affected, and you may even be included in the list of dishonest people." You have obviously never borrowed a campus loan, but the other party said that "registering an account counts" and "the country is clearing it out, and everyone has to check it." You start to panic. They call themselves "Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission", "Banking Regulatory Commission" and "Campus Loan Repayment Specialist", state your school and name, and pin you down on the chair with the words "impact on credit report" and "blacklist". "You still have a loan limit in your account. You must clear the limit before canceling, otherwise it will be regarded as a malicious loan." - This is the core of the whole scam: it allows you to lend out all the money you can borrow on the online loan platform. The other party guides you to open various online loan apps, borrow money, withdraw cash one by one, and transfer the money to the so-called "offset account" and "clearance account" (scammer's account). They provide "intimate guidance" throughout the process, and remind you "you don't need to tell your family, your credit will be cleared after completing the process." After all the credit cards, Huabei, Jiebei, and Weilidai were drained, the "CBRC staff" lost contact. Not only did you lose your money, but you also took on a bunch of online loans "signed by yourself", which made your credit investigation really expensive.
Routine: 1️⃣ Pretend to be a supervisor and create panic 2️⃣ "Clear the credit limit" rhetoric 3️⃣ "Guide" the whole process of screen sharing 4️⃣ No more money to borrow, the world disappears

Pitfalls: ❌ "To cancel a loan account, you need to clear the credit limit first" - Think about it based on common sense: Do you need to clear all the phone bills first to cancel your mobile phone number?

Warning: ⚠️ This type of scam specifically targets graduates and young people: those who have just started working, have strong credit awareness, and have no ability to discern the "national retirement policy".

Prevention method: 🛡️ The China Banking Regulatory Commission does not have the business of calling to cancel an account; personal credit information is managed by the People's Bank of China, and any statement that "cancellation of the account guarantees credit information" is a scam. 🛡️ There is no need to "cancel" accounts that do not lend money, and there is no "credit report will be affected if the limit is not cleared"; hang up directly when receiving such a call and call 96110 for verification.

Law: ⚖️ Anyone who pretends to be a staff member of a financial regulatory agency to commit fraud will be severely punished; all links in the capital chain (card dealers, drivers) that induce victims to borrow and transfer may be involved in the crime.
Xingnao: 🛑 Final reminder: Any operation that asks you to "lend out the credit and transfer it away", no matter what policy it is packaged as, will turn you into a debtor.

Case: Mr. Liu, who graduated five years ago, received a call from the China Banking Regulatory Commission, saying that he needed to cancel his campus loan otherwise his credit report would be affected. After following the instructions to borrow and transfer 20,000 yuan, he realized he had been deceived. When he called the police, he found that the scammer had blocked him.

items.title: "Pay a service fee, help you surrender the policy in full, and get the premium back through internal channels"? The end of agency surrender is that the protection is gone and the information is gone
items.core: This policy is not cost-effective. I will help you surrender the policy in full. No fees will be charged if it fails. We will only use internal channels! "In short videos and live broadcast rooms, there are more and more "legal teachers" and "surrender consultants".
body: Explanation: "This policy is not cost-effective. I will help you surrender the policy in full. No fees will be charged if it fails. We will use internal channels!" In short videos and live broadcast rooms, there are more and more "legal teachers" and "surrender consultants". Five departments including the State Administration of Financial Supervision, the Central Cyberspace Administration of China, and the Ministry of Public Security have jointly launched a crackdown in 2026: the so-called "full surrender" is a trap for those who have insurance policies in their hands. 👇 Pretend to be lawyers, legal and insurance experts, stare at your "dissatisfaction with the policy, urgent need of money, and do not understand the terms" mentality in short videos and live broadcasts, and shout "full surrender, no fees if unsuccessful, internal channels". Let you follow the same tactics and lie about "being misled in sales, signing on behalf of others, and having a history of illness", repeatedly complaining, reporting, and even forging evidence to force the insurance company to cancel the policy. If the surrender fails, a service fee will be charged first; in the process, they will trick you into handing over your ID card, bank card, insurance policy, and mobile phone number, and even induce you to hand over your mobile phone to the other party for operation. Once you really withdraw and lose the protection, your money may be induced to buy the high-commission products they recommend or illegally raise funds; your personal information may also be resold and taken out for loans. What's worse, contact is lost immediately after charging a fee. "Full policy surrender", "no need to repay loans and credit cards", "credit cleansing" and "full refund of investment advisory fees" are all false information and inconsistent with the "Insurance Law", "Credit Report Industry Management Regulations" and other laws. For formal surrender, you can directly call the official customer service of the insurance company or go to the business outlet. There is no need to spend money to find an "agent". - If you have any questions, verify them through the insurance company’s official customer service or official app, or report them to the financial regulatory authorities through formal channels; - Never give your ID card, insurance policy, bank card, or verification code to a stranger, let alone your mobile phone to others; - If you have been trapped by "agency surrender", stop transferring money, keep evidence, and call the police in time. Anyone who actively shouts "full surrender, no fees if unsuccessful, internal channels" is targeting your insurance policy and information. It doesn't cost money to do business through formal channels, and those who pay first to "protect their rights" will mostly get the second harvest.

Routines: 1️⃣ Accurate traffic, false promises 🎣 2️⃣ Teach you to make up reasons and make malicious complaints 📝 3️⃣ Charge high handling fees and steal your sensitive information 💳 4️⃣ After surrendering the policy, harvest in a row 💰

Defense: 🛡️ Correct approach
Sobering up: 🛑 Sobering summary

body: Explanation: The Ministry of Public Security reported at the anti-fraud press conference that the ten most common types of electronic fraud are - fake bill rebates, fake shopping services, fake online investment and financial management, fake reseller logistics customer service, loan credit reporting, fake transactions in online games, online dating and dating, impersonating public prosecutors, impersonating leaders' acquaintances, and ticket refunds and changes, which together account for 85% of all electronic fraud cases. But what's more important than the list is that the cheater has changed his equipment. In the past, the starting point of scams was spam text messages and harassing phone calls; now they "naturally recognize" you in social software, short video comment areas, and private messages in live broadcast rooms. Strangers take the initiative to chat, join groups, and scan QR codes. This is the new version of "unfamiliar calls." After establishing contact, the scammer will make up various reasons to get you to leave WeChat QQ and download "encrypted chat software" with a very small number of users - the anti-fraud monitoring of mainstream platforms cannot control it, and deep brainwashing is carried out in the dark. Anyone who asks you to "change the software to chat" is 99% taking you to a place where there is no monitoring. High imitation apps that imitate banks, claims, and financial management platforms, with built-in screen sharing, call transfer, and even remote control functions. Once installed, your bank card number, password, and verification code will be stolen in real time without your knowledge. Remember: Only install apps from the official app store, and do not install apps from external links. Fund control is getting tighter and tighter, and online transfers are easily intercepted and traced. Scammers instead ask you to withdraw cash, buy gold and mobile phones, and send it to a designated location through online ride-hailing, Lalamove, or errands, or arrange for a "driver" to pick it up at your door—without touching the banking system, making it much more difficult to recover losses.

Defense: 🛡️ Please set the "six don'ts" as family rules: do not answer suspicious calls from strangers, click on unfamiliar links, install unfamiliar apps, enable screen sharing, transfer money to strangers, and do not give cash to strangers who come to pick up goods.

Law: ⚖️ "Riders" who help people withdraw gold and give away gold will be punished with concealment crimes. They will be jailed if they transfer money even though they know it is a fraud. Don't do the last step of "making hundreds of dollars a day".

items.title: "Millet", cards, free skins: a new combination of deception targeting primary and secondary school students, one child was defrauded of 400,000 yuan
items.core: A 6-year-old child wanted to buy an anime badge and added the seller QQ - two weeks later, his parents' bank card was depleted by more than 70,000 yuan. This is not an isolated case: the Cyber ​​Security Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security issued a special reminder that "grain circle" scams are occurring frequently across the country.
body: Explanation: A 13-year-old child wanted to buy an anime badge and added the seller QQ - two weeks later, the parent’s bank card was depleted by more than 70,000 yuan. This is not an isolated case: the Cyber ​​Security Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security issued a special reminder that "grain circle" scams are occurring frequently across the country. The so-called "millet" (a homophone for Goods in English) refers to animation and game peripherals such as badges, stand-up cards, and cards. The unit price ranges from a few yuan to thousands. Children use their pocket money and New Year's money to "eat grain", and scammers use children as cash machines. "One box of My Little Pony card oil is 1 yuan", "Limited badges are 500 blind draws", "Free game skins and autographed photos from celebrities" - targeted delivery to children, and they can be added to the QQ group to "select" after private chat. In the name of "Registration required for purchases by minors," the child's name and ID number were asked, and then the conversation changed: "You are a minor, causing the company account to be frozen/violating platform regulations, and you will be legally responsible, and it will also affect the reputation of your parents!" Pretending to be a "policeman" issued a fake arrest warrant, and even made a video wearing a "police uniform" to threaten: "If you don't cooperate, your parents will be arrested!" The child was too scared to tell the parents - fear and shame, which is isolation. They are induced to download the conference software, enable screen sharing, use the parent’s mobile phone to open the bank app, and report the card number, balance, and verification code step by step. Two children in Wenzhou, Zhejiang were defrauded of 4,399 yuan and 17,498 yuan respectively; an 11-year-old primary school student in a certain place was defrauded of 400,000 yuan in his father's name by a "free card".

Routines: 1️⃣ Low-price fishing: post advertisements on short videos and social platforms 2️⃣ Register information to create "violations" 3️⃣ Fake police officers appear and video intimidation 4️⃣ Direct children to take their parents' mobile phones to "prove their innocence"

Pitfalls: ❌ "It is illegal for minors to purchase, and they must use their parents' mobile phones to eliminate the risk" - the emergence of all these phrases means that the scam has entered the closing stage.
Warning: ⚠️ The leader of the group "Eating Grain" takes money and runs away, and "exit the group for free" to cheat the registration information, are two other variations of this combo.

Defense: 🛡️ Parents, please do three things: manage your payment passwords and turn off password-free payments; tell your children, "Anyone online who says that minors are doing illegal things and need to use their parents' mobile phones to deal with them is 100% liars"; agree on a consumption limit so that your children dare to talk to you about "eating grain". 🛡️ Please keep in mind the "three no's" of the public security organs: they will not handle cases through online video, they will not require transfers to "safe accounts", and they will not send arrest warrants to personal mobile phones.

Law: ⚖️ Pretending to be a police officer to intimidate minors to transfer funds constitutes the crime of pretentiousness and fraud, and shall be severely punished; reselling minors’ information in batches constitutes the crime of infringement of citizens’ personal information.

Xingnao: 🛑 What a child fears most after being defrauded is not money, but being scolded - the first thing he says is always "I don't blame you", and then he calls the police to stop the payment and keeps a record of the chat. Put criticism at the back and stop loss at the front.

Case: 14-year-old Xiaojie saw an advertisement for free limited edition game skins in a QQ group. After adding friends, he used his parents’ mobile phone to scan the QR code and verify the code, and within two hours, 38,000 yuan was transferred from his father’s bank card.
items.remember: Please keep in mind the "three no's" of the public security organs: they will not handle cases through online video, they will not require transfers to "safe accounts", and they will not send arrest warrants to personal mobile phones.

items.title: The "boss" in the video asked you to transfer money? AI face-changing has defrauded the financial sector: 1.56 million, 1.86 million, 300,000
items.core: Ms. Zhang, the finance manager of a company in Xi'an, received a new number friend request from the "leader" during lunch time: the avatar was a photo of the leader, and the facial features, voice, and tone of voice on the video call were exactly the same. "Xiao Zhang, please transfer the company's money to another account. I need it urgently.
body: Explanation: Ms. Zhang, the finance manager of a company in Xi'an, received a new number friend application from the "leader" during lunch time: the avatar was a photo of the leader, and the facial features, voice, and tone of voice on the video call were exactly the same. "Xiao Zhang, please transfer the company's money to another account. I need it urgently." She transferred 1.56 million. She didn't know until the police came to the door that it was the city's first AI face-changing fraud case. The police stopped the payment in full after nine minutes of emergency payment stop. Similar cases are already lining up in Tianjin and Shanghai. Stealing address books, cracking cloud photo albums, stealing company official websites and short videos - the names, positions, photos and public speech videos of leaders and financial officers are all the raw materials for face-changing. The smaller a company is and the worse its information disclosure protection is, the easier it is to be targeted. Use AI tools to generate lifelike video calls and voice messages. Aunt Li in Tianjin received a video of her "nephew" crying about borrowing money, and when the "real person" said it to her face, she was all wary and transferred 50,000 yuan out; in another case, the scammer even took the initiative to initiate a video call to "prove his identity." Say "deposit for emergency projects" to the finance; say "nephew has difficulty with cash flow" to the elderly; say to the company manager "help transfer funds, I have transferred 3 million to you first" (attached with a forged screenshot of the transfer, and then used "delayed arrival of large amounts" as a prevarication). Every sentence is designed to fit your daily cognition. "It is related to the company's major interests, handle it immediately without delay" "Don't tell others" - urgency and isolation will leave you no time to verify with the real boss. By the time you reconcile in the work group, the money has been transferred three times on the first-level card.

Routines: 1️⃣ Information collection: your "face" has been stored long ago 2️⃣ Deep forgery: face changing + one-click generation of onomatopoeia 3️⃣ Script accurately matches identity 4️⃣ Urgent network closure
Pitfall: ❌ "How can it be true that the person in the video is fake?" - Yes, and it is the new type of fraud that currently poses the greatest threat to corporate finances.
Warning: ⚠️ Don’t trust the voice: Mr. Chen heard the voice of his "friend" borrowing 20,000 yuan, but he later learned that it was AI synthesis-the other party's account had already been stolen.

Defense method: 🛡️ Please set a strict rule for company finance: any transfer must be done by calling back the leader’s commonly used number or verifying it in person; during video calls, ask the other party to wave their hand in front of their face, press their nose, and turn their head - AI face-changing will reveal the secret under obstruction and large movements. 🛡️ Confidential positions and leadership should not expose photos, sounds, and videos on the public network; do not put company address books on public network drives.

Law: ⚖️ The use of AI face-changing to commit fraud will be punished as fraud, and if the amount is particularly large, the person will be sentenced to more than ten years; illegally obtaining citizens’ personal information and then superimposing the crime of public infringement will be punished for several crimes.

Xingnao: 🛑 In case of transfer: Call 110 immediately and report the payment account number to apply for emergency stop payment - the Xi'an case was frozen and the full amount was recovered in 9 minutes, speed is everything.

Case: Finance Xiao Wang of a company in Nanjing received a QQ message pretending to be his boss. The other party requested an emergency transfer through a fake video conference screen. Xiao Wang transferred 1.56 million yuan to the designated account in two installments without verification. He later found out that he had been deceived and called the police.

items.title: Scammers don’t want to transfer money and ask for cash: Withdraw 50,000 yuan in cash for “Didi” delivery, and hide 100,000 gold in milk powder cans
items.core: Ms. Song from Xianning, Hubei Province, withdrew 50,000 yuan in cash according to the "customer service" instructions and took a Didi to Wuhan to "recharge and activate membership cashback" - when the anti-fraud police came to her door, the money was still in her bag. Ms. Wang from Yantai was even more dangerous: she put 220,000 cash in a cardboard box and waited for the "driver" to pick it up, but was intercepted by the police on the spot.
body: Explanation: Ms. Song from Xianning, Hubei Province, withdrew 50,000 yuan in cash according to the "customer service" instructions, took a Didi car and prepared to send it to Wuhan to "recharge and activate membership cashback" - when the anti-fraud police came to the door, the money was still in her bag. Ms. Wang from Yantai was even more dangerous: she put 220,000 cash in a cardboard box and waited for the "driver" to pick it up, but was intercepted by the police on the spot. Since 2026, "online fraud + offline cash withdrawals + online ride-hailing and delivery" have been reported in many places across the country. This is an overall upgrade of deception targeting fund control. Rebates for swiping orders, fake investments, "manual part-time jobs", small rebates first to build trust - the front-end script has not changed, but the last step has changed: instead of letting you transfer money, you will be asked to go to the bank to withdraw cash, or go to a gold store to buy gold or a mobile phone. "Online banking recharges arrive slowly, while cash/gold delivery recharges arrive in seconds, and the rebates are higher." "Orders require offline deposits." - Taking advantage of your unfamiliarity with the new rules, package "cash withdrawals" into special offers. You can deliver cash or gold to a designated location through online car hailing, Lalamoul or errands; or you can make an appointment to hand it over to a "driver" at the gate of your community or at an intersection. The biker gang that Yantai police destroyed transferred more than 1.3 million yuan more than 30 times over ten days. The transfer points were specially chosen in places with a wide view, and they would run away as soon as strangers approached. In the investment disk, scammers will first transfer "other fraudulent funds" to your card, and then let you withdraw cash to buy gold and send it out - your account is passing through for stolen money, and the victim instantly becomes a suspect.

Routine: 1️⃣ The scam is still the same, the method of collecting money has changed 2️⃣ The rhetoric is packaged as "offline channels are faster" 3️⃣ Separation of people and goods, no meeting in the whole process 4️⃣ Second harvest: Turn you into a part of money laundering
Pitfalls: ❌ "Withdraw cash, buy gold, and let Didi send it over" - there is no such operation required for recharge, refund, and deposit in any formal business.

Warning: ⚠️ Drivers, errands, and couriers, please be careful: If a customer consigns a full box of cash, a large amount of gold, or looks nervous, asking more questions may break a chain. The police have explicitly called on practitioners to refuse shipment of suspicious orders and call 110.

Prevention: 🛡️ Please remember this tip: Anyone who asks you to withdraw cash, buy gold/shopping cards/mobile phones and hand them over to strangers is a scam; anyone who asks you to send cash and gold through online ride-hailing is a scam.

Law: ⚖️ A professional driver knowingly knowing that he is involved in fraud still withdraws cash and transfers it, which constitutes covering up and concealing the proceeds of the crime; if the victim participates in "receiving money and then transferring it out", he will be guilty of the same crime - don't turn yourself into a defendant from the victim.

Xingnao: 🛑 If it has been sent but not delivered: contact the platform immediately to intercept the recall and synchronize the alarm; when an old man withdraws a large amount of cash at the bank counter, his expression is abnormal, the teller will ask for verification according to the regulations, please be more careful, that is your last stop loss point.

Case: Aunt Zhang believed the lies of the "investment mentor" and withdrew 80,000 yuan in cash to hand over to the door-to-door "staff" for the so-called "offline recharge." She was stopped in time outside the branch by the anti-fraud police who had already been deployed to save her pension money.
items.remember: Please keep this in mind: Anyone who asks you to withdraw cash, buy gold/shopping cards/mobile phones and hand them over to strangers is a scam; anyone who asks you to send cash and gold through an online ride-hailing service is a scam.

items.title: "Overseas orders are booming!" Cross-border e-commerce agent operation: The store you opened is fake, the orders are fake, and only the advance money is real
items.core: Ms. Wang from Shandong met a "cross-border e-commerce agency operation company" online: it opened a store with zero threshold, and the supply and logistics were all taken care of. She only had to move her finger to confirm the order. After downloading an "overseas e-commerce platform" that is all in English, orders really kept popping up in the middle of the night. Five-star reviews came from all over the world. The first small advance payment really came with interest.
body: Explanation: Ms. Wang from Shandong met a "cross-border e-commerce agency operation company" online: it opened a store with zero threshold, and the supply and logistics were all taken care of. She only had to move her finger to confirm the order. After downloading an "overseas e-commerce platform" that was all in English, orders kept popping up in the middle of the night. Five-star reviews came from all over the world. The first small advance payment was actually cashed out with interest - until the "store exploded" and she needed to pay 220,000 in advance for the purchase. She withdrew the cash and waited for delivery, but was stopped by the police on the spot. After investigation, it was found that the App was a fake platform created by a fraud gang. Orders, logistics, and positive reviews were all generated in the background. Advertisements are placed on short videos and social platforms, with fake platform qualifications and screenshots of "hot orders" in the backend of the store, specifically looking for people who want to start a side business but don't understand cross-border e-commerce. Click the link to download the unofficial "Cross-border E-commerce App", and the "Operation Tutor" will teach you one-on-one to register a store and put products on the shelves. The process is so professional that you won't be suspicious - from this step on, you have entered the scammer's server. Advance 500 yuan to purchase a "small order", and the principal plus 200 profit will be credited to your account in seconds, and you can also withdraw cash. This step is not to deceive you 500, but to deceive you the next 220,000. The more orders are received, the more advance payments are made; then "big benefits" are offered: the more deposits are made in advance, the higher the commissions are, and "the more you recharge, the company will give you a mobile phone or a car." Finally, the "explosion" comes - the pre-deposit is not enough, and the company "kindly" helps you advance as long as you make up the cash. Either a large amount of cash is handed over to the "rider" offline, or it is found that the account cannot be withdrawn, and the "customer service" continues to collect unfreezing fees, deposits, and taxes until the App cannot be logged in and all contacts are lost.

Routine: 1️⃣ Advertising traffic: "Open a store with zero foundation, no need to stock up, monthly income of hundreds of thousands" 2️⃣ High imitation platform + mentor to accompany you 3️⃣ Small amount to test the waters, real rebates 4️⃣ Backstage orders are huge, bottomless pit of advance payment 5️⃣ Closing the network: offline delivery or cash withdrawal freeze
Pitfalls: ❌ "When overseas buyers place an order, you only need to pay for the goods in advance" - this sentence is the key to the whole scam. You should quit when you hear it.

Warning: ⚠️ There are three variants: TikTok store "short video sales sharing", "professional agent operation" that only charges high service fees, and MLM-style fission that develops downline commissions.

Defense: 🛡️ If you want to do cross-border e-commerce, please only download real platform apps (Amazon, Shopee, TikTok Shop official) through official app stores, and never trust private links; platforms with profit margins of "20% for silver members, 30% for gold members" are mathematically false. 🛡️ Please keep in mind: Zero threshold and high returns are all scams; deposits, deposits, advance payments, and "paying money first" in any name are all scams.

Law: ⚖️ Building a false trading platform to defraud advance funds constitutes a crime of fraud. The 280 million yuan-level market involved in the case was treated as a "particularly large amount"; the "driver" who collected and paid on behalf of the company was punished with a crime of concealment.

Xingnao: 🛑 For those who have advanced payment but have not "exploded the order": stop all additional additions, keep the App screen recording, transfer records, and tutor chat records and call the police immediately - Ms. Zhang from Anji, Huzhou was stopped by the early warning call before adding 200,000 yuan.

Case: Ms. Huang, a self-employed business owner, joined the "Cross-border E-commerce Agent Operation" and opened a store on a fake overseas platform according to the instructions. The advance payment can be withdrawn in cash. After she invested 150,000 yuan in "exploding orders and stocking up", the platform was closed and the contact disappeared.
items.remember: Please keep in mind: Zero threshold and high returns are all scams; deposits, deposits, advance payments, and "paying money first" in any name are all scams.

items.title: "AI data labeling, daily income of 200 to 500, can be done if you can type"? A part-time job where you pay a deposit first, the familiar smell comes again
items.core: During the outbreak, there is a huge shortage of data annotators. You can make hundreds of dollars a day with just a few clicks at home, and you can do it with zero foundation! "
body: Explanation: "AI has exploded, and there is a huge shortage of data annotators. With just a few clicks at home, you can make hundreds of dollars a day, and you can do it with zero foundation!" In 2026, many people were attracted by the "AI data annotation" advertisement. As a result, once the deposit and membership fee were paid, the task could not be completed at all, and the money could not be withdrawn. There are also people who were tricked into taking the "National Certified AI Engineer Certificate", only to find out that it was waste paper. 👇 "Copywriting rewriting, picture annotation, voice transcription, daily income of 200 to 500", the threshold is said to be extremely low and the income is extremely high. There are a lot of reasons: "system usage fee", "training deposit", "order qualification fee", ranging from a few hundred to two thousand - the routine of paying first is the same as that of order brushing and typists. If you actually take the order, the tasks are many and difficult (such as labeling thousands of blurry pictures), and the "pass rate and time limit" are deliberately set so that you can never meet the settlement standards. "The AI ​​engineer certificate certified by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and recognized by the country can make money with certification and affiliation." The fees are tens of thousands. The certificate is purely fictitious and the affiliation is a scam. Once the money is collected, the app cannot be opened and the customer service loses contact; some even engage in "development downline commissions" and slide into pyramid schemes. Formal data annotation and AI training work will be recruited through formal platforms or companies. You will not be asked to pay a deposit or training fee first, nor will you be "guaranteed or sold a certificate." All part-time jobs with "high salary, zero threshold, and payment up front", whether packaged as AI or something else, are just old scams. Remember the iron rule: any part-time job that asks you to pay up front is a scam. Don't believe the so-called "national certification and internal certificates" if you can't find official records.
Chapter: 📌 [Shadow Exposure] AI Data Labeling Scam Routines

Sobering up: 🛑 Sobering summary

items.title: "Two mobile phones and one cable, a daily salary of 600": high-paying part-time "mobile phone operators", the people sentenced are all around 20 years old
items.core: Xiaohai, a 17-year-old high school student in Xinjiang, came across a part-time job advertisement on the forum: "Two mobile phones and one cable, living in a big hotel every day." The online "Nikebao" remotely taught him to set up the equipment, gave him a QR code, two mobile phones, a recording line, and a phone card to form a simple GOIP - overseas fraudsters use it to dial the phone number displayed as a "local number"
body: Explanation: Xiaohai, a 17-year-old high school student in Xinjiang, saw a part-time job advertisement on the forum: "Two mobile phones and one cable, staying in a big hotel every day." The online "Nikebao" remotely taught him to set up the equipment, gave him a QR code, two mobile phones, a recording line, and a phone card to form a simple GOIP - which overseas fraudsters use to make calls that appear as "local numbers." Xiaohai "earned" 86,000 yuan in three months, at the cost of helping Xinxin be sentenced to one year in prison. A Shandong Liu with a "daily salary of 600" helped the scammer answer three calls. Three victims were defrauded of 130,000 yuan, and he became an accomplice in the crime of fraud. "The hourly wage for two mobile phones is 200-300", "You only need to change cards to listen to calls and get paid every day" and "You can make money just lying down at home" - the distribution channels are short video comment areas, part-time groups, and forums, and the targets are students and young people who are new to society and are tight on money. One mobile phone uses social software to connect to overseas scammers, the other plugs in a local calling card to call the domestic victim, and the audio lines of the two phones are connected (or hands-free is turned on) - the overseas call becomes a "local call" in your city. Liu could hear the other party pretending to be the charger's customer service to defraud him, and saw the dialed number - legally "knowingly" was established from this moment on. The so-called "I just provided the mobile phone" was never a defense in the judgment. Use USDT to settle and then find a channel to cash out, and both the money and the crime will remain in your name: the equipment is at your home, the card was issued by you, and the proceeds went into your account - the police found you along the way, and the scammer and the "upline" have long since changed their vests.

Routines: 1️⃣ Advertising language: packaging crime as a part-time job 2️⃣ Fool-proof equipment: a "mobile phone port" for recording lines 3️⃣ You can hear every fraudulent call 4️⃣ Reward virtual currency settlement, arbitrarily determine your retreat
Pitfall: ❌ "I'm just doing a small favor, it's not a crime, right?" - There is no exemption for "helping" in the filing standards for the crime of trust.

Warning: ⚠️ The same traps include: renting out phone and bank cards, helping people "manage mobile phones" to run data traffic, collecting and delivering GOIP equipment for door-to-door installation - all in different stations on the same chain.

Defense: 🛡️ Please make this an iron law: any "part-time job" that requires you to provide your mobile phone, phone card, and payment code will always rent you to a criminal gang. The higher the daily wage, the longer the sentence. 🛡️ Attention parents of students: Extra recording lines, unfamiliar phone cards, and "salaries" from unknown sources in their children's rooms are all danger signs.

Law: ⚖️ The crime of aiding and trusting can be punished by up to three years; when the circumstances are upgraded to the crime of concealment, the crime can be punished by up to seven years; those like Liu who knowingly knowing the specific fraud but still assisting will be directly treated as an accomplice in the crime of fraud - the three levels of punishment, the starting point is the "daily salary of 600" recording line.

Xingnao: 🛑 Those who have already participated: stop immediately, keep all records, and voluntarily surrender - surrendering and returning the stolen property is a legally lenient circumstance. The difference between Shan, who was sentenced to one year and six months, and Qiang Qiang, who was suspended, is taking the initiative and being caught.

Case: In order to earn a part-time job with a daily salary of 600 yuan, 19-year-old Xiao Liu used two mobile phones and a data cable to set up a "mobile phone port" device in a hotel room to assist overseas fraud dens in making fraudulent calls. He was later detained by the police for helping.

body: Explanation: It is not the kind of gold that you buy gold bars and put at home - it is "gold on the platform". "Gold fights inflation" and "the price of gold will soar when the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates" - using the real gold market as bait to lead you to a fake platform. Make money by recharging a small amount to buy up or down, and you can withdraw money in seconds. Some people mortgage their properties to make additional investments, while others are pulled into online loans to "buy the dip." Overnight, the app could not be opened, the website showed 404, and the "customer service" avatar was all gray. Even the screenshot of your account balance when you reported the crime was the last fake number shown to you by the backend.

items.title: You can receive hundreds of thousands of "national poverty alleviation funds" by paying a few hundred yuan in "activation fees"? Revealing why the old scam of "unfreezing national assets" took away another 6 billion

body: Explanation: If an elder in the family posts "national secret projects", "national assets will be unfrozen immediately", "you can receive hundreds of thousands of donations by paying a construction fee" in the group, don't take it as a joke and hold down his phone first! This is an old scam that has been going on for decades, but it changes every year and people believe it every year. In September 2026, the Ministry of Public Security specially announced: a batch of false investment projects in the "unfreezing of national assets" category, involving a total amount of up to 6 billion yuan! 👇 The scammers talk about "Revival Huijin", "Old Age Care Action", "China's Strengthening Agriculture" and "People's Livelihood Security", which all sound like national affairs. Coupled with forged red-headed documents, red official seals, screenshots of leaders' speeches, and even a specially made copycat app, the air of "national project" was fully displayed, and the old man was in awe at the first sight. If you want to participate in "receiving money", you must first pay "startup fee, membership fee, production fee, and file fee", ranging from tens to hundreds of dollars. Just because he didn't have much money, the old man spent his money without any precautions. Scammers will also issue "membership cards" and "donation vouchers" to make you feel like you are "in the system." Every time someone is brought in, there is a commission, and the group also arranges for "old members" to post "screenshots of donations" they have received (all shills). In order to "get an extra share", the old man brought in all his old sisters and colleagues, and unknowingly became a free publicity agent for the scammer. The scammer promised that once the assets are unfrozen, each member can receive hundreds of thousands or even millions of "resettlement fees and poverty alleviation funds." But the "unfreezing day" is always pushed back - "the country is still operating secretly", "the time has not come yet", "paying a confidentiality fee will make you eligible". It was not until the group owner logged out and the app could not be opened that the old man discovered that not a penny was true from beginning to end. Scammers love to target short video comment areas, WeChat groups, and family groups, specifically targeting people who are short of money and hoping that "the country can send money." Remember a common sense: the state's subsidies, poverty alleviation funds, and relief funds are all processed directly through grassroots organizations, civil affairs departments, and your own bank card. You will never be asked to pay "cost of production and start-up fees" first, and there are no "secretly unfrozen national assets." The principal offenders of this type of scam are usually held criminally responsible for the crime of fraud and organizing and leading pyramid schemes. If the amount involved is particularly huge, they may be sentenced to more than ten years in prison or even life imprisonment. The so-called "national assets" are either fictitious or "legacy of the previous dynasty and overseas treasures" fabricated by swindlers, none of which is true. Anyone who asks you to pay money first and then receive "national poverty alleviation funds, national charity funds, and unfrozen funds" is 100% a scam. If you see this kind of news forwarded in an elder group, don’t criticize, just show him the notice from the Ministry of Public Security, and then help him withdraw from the group or block him.

Financial regulatory authorities in Beijing, Chongqing and other places have successively reminded: Some people package AI pictures worth a few yuan into "limited collections", and then run away with the money after the hype! 👇 Freely downloaded pictures and AI-generated pictures from the Internet are packaged as "museum co-branded, officially authorized, limited edition number", and coupled with forged cooperation certificates. "After buying, the platform repurchases it at a high price" and "holding it will earn dividends", giving you the illusion of making a sure profit without losing money. The platform uses a large number of small accounts to repeatedly buy and sell, pushing the price higher and higher, and increasing the trading volume to lure you into the market. When you take over the market at a high level, the platform will either shut down and run away, or set up a "transfer lock-up period, high handling fees, and withdrawal thresholds" so that the "collection" in your hand cannot be sold at all and you cannot get your money back. Others engage in pyramid schemes under the guise of digital collections, attracting customers and offering hierarchical rebates. Digital collections do not have financial attributes in China, and regulation clearly prohibits speculation, and no promises of repurchase or profit are allowed. A picture that can be copied indefinitely is sold at a high price based on the promise of "scarcity", and the person who finally takes over is destined to lose everything. Any digital collection that promises "guaranteed repurchase, doubling of the price, and dividends" is illegal fundraising or fraud. Don’t gamble with real money if you can’t understand or tell the value of something.

Sobering up: 🛑 Sobering summary

Soon after, the platform was closed, customer service lost contact, and the so-called Yuanverse land was in vain, with a total loss of principal.

items.title: "Invest in a vending machine, earn high monthly dividends, and the company will fully manage"? , the harvest is for you who want to start a business
items.core: I will negotiate the location of the vending machine, I will replenish the goods, and I will maintain the machine. You just invest money, and you will get a share every month. The quota is limited! "
body: Explanation: "I will negotiate the location of the vending machine, I will replenish the goods, and I will maintain the machine. You just invest the money, and you will get a commission every month. The quota is limited! " Unmanned retail sounds like a worry-free business, but in 2026, entrepreneurs continued to complain: after paying the franchise fee, the machine disappeared, the points were fake, and the company turned against the person when they wanted to refund the money. 👇 "You can earn several thousand per month with one machine" "You can do it with no experience, and the headquarters will support you throughout the process", and you will also receive other people's "profit statements" to make you feel that you are making a sure profit. Once the money is handed over, what you get may be inferior and refurbished machines. The so-called "golden points" either do not exist or have been eliminated long ago. How many goods were sold and how much money was earned are all numbers shown to you by the platform's backend, and you cannot verify them at all. When you find out that you have lost money and want to return the machine, the company says that "buyback is just a negotiation, not an obligation." The withdrawal mechanism and liability for breach of contract are vague in the contract, making it even more difficult to protect your rights. What's more, after receiving the money, the company will be canceled directly and the building will be empty. Unmanned retail is not a business that can be easily earned. You have to worry about ordering, product selection, replenishment, and maintenance. You must keep money and equipment in your own hands. Those with "advanced financial platform accounts, unclear equipment property rights, and completely locked operations" are extremely risky. Before joining, ask questions: whose account the money goes into, who owns the equipment, who can see the data, and how to withdraw money. Don't believe the propaganda of "full custody, high commission, and guaranteed profit", and don't pay before you see the real point.
Chapter: 📌 [Shadow Exposure] Routine of Vending Machine Franchise Scam

Routine: 1️⃣ "Low investment, high return, full trusteeship" picture 🤖 2️⃣ Collect high franchise fees, equipment fees, deposits 💸 3️⃣ Operations are all based on one mouth, data is falsified 📊 4️⃣ The buy-back terms are in name only, and there is no way to get a refund 🚪

However, the equipment was a second-hand refurbished machine and there was very little foot traffic at the location. After three months, the company lost contact. He had to rely on himself for maintenance and replenishment, and lost all his money.
